subject: german
title: Stamp 1: The Energiewende
welcome_lead: Stamp Germany's energy transition to renewables.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on the Energiewende, nuclear phaseout, and renewables.

concepts.def: Energy transition; shift away from fossil fuels and nuclear towards renewables.
Nuclear phaseout; final shutdown of remaining nuclear reactors in April 2023.
Renewable energies: wind, solar, biomass, hydropower.
Erneuerbare-Energien-Gesetz 2000; law guaranteeing fixed prices for renewable electricity.
Wind power; major component of renewable generation, especially in northern Lander.
Goal of climate neutrality by 2045, tightened from earlier 2050 target.

walkthroughs.body_html: The term Energiewende dates from the 1980s but became official policy under Merkel after Fukushima (2011). Germany committed to phasing out nuclear and expanding renewables.
The 2000 EEG guaranteed feed-in tariffs for renewable electricity, sparking a solar and wind boom. Renewables now generate over half of German electricity in many months.
After Fukushima, Merkel reversed her own 2010 extension of nuclear plant lifespans. The last three reactors (Isar 2, Emsland, Neckarwestheim 2) shut down on 15 April 2023.
